settings.note: CUDA / HIP, not a user setting. Unset: the HIP cards gfx1030 / gfx1031 / gfx1032 (RX 6000 series RDNA2, no matrix cores) run a prompt layer's expert groups on our own int8 dot-product kernels (native_expert_i8) for the gate/up formats IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S and IQ2_S with an IQ4_NL or Q2_0 down, in the prompt path's MMQ groups of 256 entries or more (include/strata/kernels/i8_expert_rule.hpp); every other card is unchanged in a build with MMQ. In a build without llama.cpp's MMQ (-DSTRATA_MMQ=OFF, or HIP without STRATA_PREFILL_MMQ) unset means on for every card and every layer the kernel covers that the fused kernels and the staged group entry do not take (otherwise the layer would run on the per-expert FP16 path); on a Tesla P100 (compute capability 6.0, no dp4a) that default applies only to prompt chunks under the stream floor (stream_all_min, 1,024 tokens), the FP16 path from it up, as the build with MMQ does there. =0 goes back to the old kernels on that class, or to the FP16 path in a build without MMQ (the way back). =1 asks for the int8 kernels on any card (a layer the fused kernels take stays on them; on a card with fused kernels set STRATA_PF_FUSED=0 as well) . The Qwen3.6 engine (strata-q36) asks the same question per layer (include/strata/kernels/q36_prompt_route.hpp): the fused kernels, then these kernels when this is set to 1, then MMQ, then these kernels when it is not 0, then the grouped kernels; the gate/up formats Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K and Q8_0 with a Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 or Q5_1 down are covered there, and a chunk whose experts average under 7 rows (6 on a P100) takes the grouped kernels. Goes away with MMQ (release C) or stays as the only path.
